label: BW-style / CLI-adapted

rubric_scores.evidence: The kitchen run, upper cabinets, extractor, cooktop, rear dark inset, slatted wall, white door and low black-and-white unit clearly reproduce the main scene identity. The sink is substantially simplified.
The kitchen remains on the right, with cabinets above the counter, cooktop forward of the rear inset, and the low unit left of the door on the slatted back wall.

The counter and upper cabinets are excessively deep relative to the door and working height. The counter depth is 1.80 against a door-panel width of 0.78 and counter height near 0.93; the broad worktop and oversized hob visibly depart from the reference proportions.
Brown cabinetry and timber slats, pale stone and backsplash, white door, and dark appliances preserve the main color and surface organization despite simplified finishes.
The authored composition is sufficiently illuminated to identify all major elements. Lighting is flatter and less locally warm than the reference, but does not obscure the required content.
Complementary views show cabinet depth, counter thickness, floor perspective and changing occlusion, establishing a volumetric scene. The blank wide_01 view does not negate the clear views.

Actual mesh objects provide separately addressable architecture, slats, door, low unit and kitchen components. Representative objects have finite nonempty meshes, assigned materials and parent chains; material nodes connect to surface outputs.

dimension_scores.evidence: The distinctive kitchen and slatted-wall composition is recognizable, though counter proportions, sink detail and surface character differ.
Major furnishings appear supported and cabinetry connects coherently. The sink reads as a flat surface insert rather than a usable basin, and cabinet construction is rudimentary.
The warm wood, white surfaces and black accents correspond well; uniform cabinet faces and prominent burner outlines reduce stylistic fidelity.
Heavy visible render noise, sharp box geometry, flat sink treatment and sparse construction detail make the delivered result look preliminary.
Main left/right, front/back and vertical relationships are retained, with a more expansive worktop and circulation area.
Door and low unit are plausible, but the unusually deep counter and upper cabinetry, large hob and tall working gap weaken relative scale.
Lighting maintains legibility and broad surface contrasts, but noise and weak local illumination flatten the reference's warmer, more differentiated atmosphere.
Most major visible elements are represented, including the extractor and wall fittings; basin depth, drainer detail and cabinet articulation remain simplified.

same_model_bias_limit: Research and independent judge use Astra; separate sessions do not establish human independence.
